item.title: Bonding‐chemistry‐guided design of carbon frameworks for rechargeable‐ion batteries
item.description:
این مقاله با رویکرد شیمی پیوند، چارچوبی اتمی برای طراحی چارچوبهای کربنی باتریهای قابل شارژ ارائه میدهد و ساختار کربن را به رفتار الکتروشیمیایی مرتبط میکند.
InfoMat | 💭 Perspective | 🔓 Open Access
💡 This perspective introduces bonding chemistry as a unified, atom-level framework linking carbon structure to electrochemical behavior in rechargeable-ion batteries. It uniquely integrates C/C hybridization, carbon-heteroatom interactions, and dynamic ion-framework bonding, establishing bond-descriptor-based design principles that connect synthesis to storage thermodynamics, kinetics, and reversibility—enabling more systematic, predictive carbon framework engineering.
🏷 carbon framework · bonding chemistry · rechargeable-ion battery · ion storage · structure-property relationship

item.title: Air Sensitivity and Surface Residual Alkali in Sodium‐Ion Layered Oxide Cathodes: A Review
item.description:

Advanced Energy Materials | ⭐ Review
💡 This review uniquely addresses air sensitivity and residual alkali in sodium-ion layered oxide cathodes, highlighting sodium-specific challenges absent in lithium-ion systems: NaHCO₃ formation, severe Na⁺/H⁺ exchange, and narrow processing windows. It bridges formation mechanisms, characterization, and modification strategies, offering future perspectives to guide practical, air-stable, high-performance cathode development.
🏷 sodium-ion battery · layered oxide cathode · residual alkali · air sensitivity · surface degradation

Advanced Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This work uniquely converts residual rock-salt reconstruction on spent NCM cathodes into a protective F-enriched interphase via molten-salt relithiation and fluorine treatment. It enables stable 4.6 V cycling (80.28% retention after 400 cycles) by strengthening Ni─O bonds and raising oxygen-vacancy formation energy, offering a high-value upcycling route for spent layered oxide cathodes.

item.description:

Energy & Environmental Science | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This study unveils phase synergy and heterogeneity in biphasic sodium layered oxide cathodes, addressing the poor long-term stability that hinders commercial adoption of low-cost Ni–Mn–Fe oxide sodium-ion batteries. By revealing how coexisting phases interact, it provides mechanistic insight to guide rational design of durable, sustainable cathodes, advancing sodium-ion technology as a viable alternative to lithium-ion systems.

item.title: Stereochemical origin of potential hysteresis in lithium metal batteries with lithium-rich cation-disordered rocksalt positive electrodes
item.description:

Nature Nanotechnology | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This study reveals that multiscale stereochemistry—atomic-scale distortion and nanoscale short-range ordering—governs potential hysteresis in Li||DRX cells. Redox-inactive d0 transition metals, via the pseudo Jahn–Teller effect, weaken Ni–O charge transfer and enhance lattice oxygen redox reversibility. This insight enables rational design of DRX electrodes with reduced hysteresis and improved energy efficiency.
🏷 lithium metal battery · cation-disordered rocksalt · hysteresis · stereochemistry · positive electrode

💡 This study first applies machine-learning potentials to glassy antiperovskite Li2OHBr0.5Cl0.5, revealing fast ion conduction mechanisms inaccessible to prior methods. It identifies lattice compliance and a partial paddlewheel mechanism as key drivers, linking amorphization to enhanced ionic transport. This advances rational design of superionic solid electrolytes for next-generation batteries.

item.title: Tuning the d-Band Center via High-Entropy-Induced Lattice Strain Enables Reversible Nanosheet-like Li2O2 Electrocatalysis
item.description:

💡 High-entropy sulfide (CoFeNiMnZn)₃S₄ introduces lattice strain that tunes the d-band center, optimizing intermediate adsorption. This yields nanosheet-like Li₂O₂ instead of film/toroid products, enabling reversible Li–O₂ batteries with 17874 mAh g⁻¹ capacity, 0.57 V overpotential, and 420+ cycles. It establishes a new paradigm for high-entropy electrocatalyst design.

💡 Directly integrating calcium nitrate tetrahydrate PCM as both latent-heat medium and working fluid inside an oscillating heat pipe creates a fully passive battery thermal management system. It cuts thermal resistance 30%, keeps cell temperature differences under 4.2°C, lowers exergy losses, and raises predicted ROI to 48.4%, offering an energy-efficient, economically attractive solution for fast-charging lithium-ion batteries.

Significance: achieves 1.46 W cm⁻² peak power and only 14.4% degradation after 30,000 cycles, offering a general route to durable fuel cell electrocatalysts.
